condition: Ovarian torsion in a premenarchal girl
permutationLabel: Premenarchal 11-year-old, labelled gastroenteritis, Doppler flow present
summary: 11-year-old premenarchal girl (38 kg), 18 h intermittent lower abdominal pain and vomiting labelled "gastroenteritis"; US: enlarged left ovary with peripheral follicles and a whirlpool sign, arterial flow still present. Doppler flow does not exclude torsion.

inputs.hpi: Premenarchal 11-year-old girl with 18 hours of intermittent severe lower abdominal pain, worse on the left, vomiting six times. Seen at a health centre last night and told it was gastroenteritis; no diarrhoea. Pain comes in waves and makes her cry. No fever, no urinary symptoms.

exam.general: Distressed between waves of pain. T 37.4, HR 118, BP 108/66.
exam.abdomen: Tender left iliac fossa and suprapubic region with guarding; no rebound.

imaging.name: USS abdomen and pelvis (transabdominal)
imaging.result: Left ovary enlarged 6.2 cm with peripheralised follicles and a twisted vascular pedicle (whirlpool sign); arterial Doppler flow present. Small free fluid. Appendix normal calibre.

inputs.socialHistory: Primary school pupil, lives with parents.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Left ovarian torsion
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Left ovarian torsion in a premenarchal girl (whirlpool sign; Doppler flow present does not exclude torsion). Emergency laparoscopy and detorsion with ovarian preservation; paediatric surgery / gynaecology.

mustExclude.note: Weight 38 kg. Paracetamol 1 g, ibuprofen 400 mg, piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g, co-amoxiclav 1.2 g, meropenem 1 g, morphine 2.5–5 mg, ondansetron 4 mg and fixed 1 L, 1–2 L or 500 mL fluid volumes are adult fixed doses; a child needs weight-based (mg/kg, mL/kg) dosing. Prescribing accuracy is a patient-safety issue, so critical.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Give protocol medications and prompt templates an age/weight branch (mg/kg and mL/kg with an adult maximum) and suppress fixed adult doses when age < 16 or weight < 50 kg; use age-specific vital-sign ranges before firing the adult shock/sepsis/tachycardia prompts.

mustExclude.note: Oophorectomy is not the default; ACOG favours preservation even when the ovary looks non-viable.

guideline.name: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 783 — adnexal torsion in adolescents
guideline.section: Torsion is a surgical emergency: prompt laparoscopy; preserve the ovary (detorsion) even when it looks non-viable, rather than oophorectomy; normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion
guideline.citation: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. Adnexal torsion in adolescents: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 783. Obstet Gynecol. 2019;134:e56–e63.

rationale: Adnexal torsion in girls is frequently mislabelled as gastroenteritis; preserved Doppler flow does not exclude it. Prompt laparoscopy with ovarian preservation and weight-based analgesia are required.
